draft.title: Venn diagrams
card: A Venn diagram uses overlapping circles inside a box. Each circle holds the outcomes for one event. The box holds every outcome in the sample space.
the overlap, where an outcome is in both circles.
everything in at least one of the circles, including the overlap.

everything outside a circle. The region inside the box but outside every circle is neither event. Example: 30 students, 12 play netball, 9 play soccer, 4 play both. Neither is \(30 - (8 + 4 + 5) = 13\).
draft.remember: Fill the overlap first, then the rest of each circle, then the outside. Probability is the count in a region over the total.

a.q: In a Year 9 class of 30, 12 play netball, 9 play soccer and 4 play both. How many play neither sport?
a.why: Netball only is \(12 - 4 = 8\) and soccer only is \(9 - 4 = 5\). Netball or soccer is \(8 + 4 + 5 = 17\) students, so neither is \(30 - 17 = 13\). Adding \(12 + 9 = 21\) counts the 4 who play both twice.
a.clue: Count each student once, then subtract from 30.

b.q: Of 40 people at a Dubbo gym, 18 use the pool, 15 use the weights room and 6 use both. A person is chosen at random. What is the probability they use the pool or the weights room?
b.why: Pool only is 12 and weights only is 9. Pool or weights is \(12 + 6 + 9 = 27\) people, so the probability is \(\frac{27}{40}\). Adding \(18 + 15 = 33\) counts the 6 in both twice.
b.clue: The overlap should be counted only once.

proposal.title: Venn diagrams
card: A Venn diagram has overlapping circles inside a box. Each circle holds the outcomes of one event. The box holds every outcome in the sample space, and the region outside every circle is neither event.
\(A\) and \(B\) is the overlap, in both circles. \(A\) or \(B\) is everything in at least one circle, with the overlap counted once. Not \(A\) is everything outside circle \(A\).

Fill the overlap first, then subtract it from each circle's total to get the only parts. Example: of 30 students, 12 play netball, 9 play soccer and 4 play both. Netball only is \(12 - 4 = 8\) and soccer only is \(9 - 4 = 5\).
Neither is \(30 - (8 + 4 + 5) = 13\). A probability is the count in a region over the total, so \(P(\text{neither}) = \frac{13}{30}\).
proposal.remember: Count the overlap once. Probability is the count in a region over the total.

a.q: In a group of 32 students, 15 study French, 11 study Japanese and 5 study both. How many study neither language?
a.why: French only is \(15 - 5 = 10\) and Japanese only is \(11 - 5 = 6\). At least one language is \(10 + 5 + 6 = 21\), so neither is \(32 - 21 = 11\). Subtracting \(15 + 11 = 26\) gives 6, which counts the 5 in both twice.
a.clue: Find the only parts first, and count each student once.

b.q: Of 40 people at a Dubbo gym, 18 use the pool, 15 use the weights room and 6 use both. A person is chosen at random. What is the probability they use the pool or the weights room?
b.why: Pool only is \(18 - 6 = 12\) and weights only is \(15 - 6 = 9\). Pool or weights is \(12 + 6 + 9 = 27\) people, so the probability is \(\frac{27}{40}\). Adding \(18 + 15 = 33\) counts the 6 in both twice.
b.clue: Or includes the overlap, but only once.
